snip.t: Hypovolaemic shock: Over‑diuresis or albumin loss leading to intravascular depletion despite peripheral oedema — Tachycardia, hypotension, renal hypoperfusion — Acute, often after aggressive diuretic regimens
| Hypovolaemic shock | Dehydration, haemorrhage, flat JVP, dry mucosa | Clear lungs, rapid response to fluid challenge |
Hypovolaemic shock – multi‑organ failure, high mortality if not rapidly corrected.
If uncorrected, this fluid shift causes profound hypovolaemic shock.
Proximal fluid accumulation leads to severe dehydration, electrolyte disturbances, and hypovolaemic shock.
Distinguish from haemorrhagic (hypovolaemic) shock, which gives tachycardia and cold peripheries.
